name: Track equipment insurance
summary: Every lease requires the customer to insure the equipment with the company named as loss payee, and a team of four insurance tracking coordinators checks that they do. They set up a tracking record for each new contract, review certificates of insurance sent by customers and brokers, chase corrections, follow up policies that expire or are cancelled, and enrol customers who never send proof in the company's protection program, which adds a monthly charge to the invoice and is reported to the program insurer each month. Most certificates are checked in minutes, but about a third are wrong (wrong business name, no loss payee wording, missing equipment) and lapse cases take one to two months of letters and waiting before enrolment.

baseline.org_archetype: A mid-size Canadian independent equipment lessor with about 55,000 active contracts, an in-house insurance tracking team using a tracking database linked to the lease system, and a protection program underwritten by an outside insurer.
baseline.notes: Certificates arrive by e-mail, fax and mail as CSIO-style certificates of property insurance. Letters are generated in daily batches by the tracker. Tracking is in-house, although many lessors outsource it to tracking vendors.

trigger: A newly booked contract, a certificate of insurance or renewal from a customer, broker or customer service, or a tracker alert that a policy has expired or been cancelled.
end_state: Compliant coverage is recorded with its expiry date, the customer is enrolled in the protection program with the charge set up and reported to the insurer, a loss is passed to lease administration, or the alert is closed.

volume.seasonality: Renewal certificates peak at the start of the year and at common policy renewal dates; new contract set-ups follow bookings.

evidence.note: Organisation file process map, driven by about 55,000 active contracts: about 1,400 new contracts a month plus renewals on contracts insured by customers and lapse cases.

All four coordinators in the organisation file work only on this process. The step times imply about 5 FTE of coordinator hands-on work at 4,400 cases a month, so the team runs with a backlog or the organisation file is about one coordinator short. Cost from the organisation file.
Approvals of waivers and backdated credits, the monthly bordereau and queue management; the rest of the supervisor's time is staff and program administration. Cost from the organisation file.
Calls from customers who see a protection program charge on their invoice, about 20% of enrolments. Cost from the organisation file.

systems.name: Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
Document imaging and contract file store
Spreadsheet models (pool cuts, borrowing base, covenants, budget, tax workpapers)
Contact centre telephony and shared mailboxes
Vendor and broker application portal with origination workflow and document generation

steps.name: Sort the insurance inbox and tracker work schedule
steps.description: A coordinator works the shared insurance mailbox, fax queue and scanned mail (certificates from brokers and customers, certificates forwarded by customer service, cancellation notices, loss reports) and the tracker's daily work schedule of newly booked contracts and policies reaching expiry, and sends each item to the right type of work.

error.defect_description: Item sorted to the wrong contract or work type.

evidence.note: A daily work schedule of accounts per clerk is the documented tracker design. The mix of work types is a tier C estimate from about 1,400 bookings a month and annual renewals on contracts with customer insurance.

steps.name: Set up the tracking record for a new contract
steps.description: For a contract booked overnight the coordinator opens the tracker record created from the booking, checks the equipment, serial numbers, cost and required coverage against the insurance requirement documentation entered, and looks for a certificate already received before funding. If one is on file it is linked; if not the contract goes into the request cycle.

error.defect_description: Coverage amount or equipment list set up wrongly.

evidence.note: Based on the booking step that sets the insurance requirement and program flag (efc-book-contracts s12) and the requirement letter sent with documents (efc-prepare-lease-documents s18).

steps.name: Match the certificate to the contract and index it
steps.description: The coordinator identifies the customer and contracts the certificate covers (brokers often omit the contract number and list a different business name), searches the tracker and lease system, and indexes the image to each contract in the imaging system.

error.defect_description: Certificate indexed to the wrong contract of the same customer.

evidence.note: Matching difficulty is the author's estimate; the organisation file notes certificates that list the wrong insured are common.

steps.name: Review the certificate against the requirement
steps.description: The coordinator compares the certificate with the contract's requirement: the named insured matches the lessee, the company is shown as loss payee (and additional insured for liability where required), the equipment is described by serial number or as all leased equipment, the limit covers replacement value, the deductible is within the maximum, the dates are current and the insurer is licensed. Certificates that only say additional insured, list the wrong business or omit units are sent back.

error.defect_description: A certificate with the wrong insured or no loss payee wording is accepted.

control.basis: Lease insurance clause and credit policy: all-risk property cover for replacement value with the company as loss payee, liability cover naming the company as additional insured

next.condition: contract already paid out or closed

evidence.note: Requirements and certificate wording issues are described in the sources. The 32% deficiency rate is a tier C estimate.

steps.name: Approve a waiver or non-standard coverage
steps.description: The supervisor reviews requests to accept something other than the standard: a fleet customer's blanket policy without serial numbers, a high deductible, self-insurance by a strong mid-ticket customer or a certificate from an unlicensed or foreign insurer, checks the credit file and the equipment value, and approves, approves with conditions or declines.

control.basis: Insurance and credit policy: delegated authority for insurance waivers and self-insurance

evidence.note: Self-insurance for creditworthy clients is described in the prospectus; times and shares are tier C.

steps.name: Record the coverage and expiry date in the tracker
steps.description: The coordinator keys the insurer, policy number, limit, deductible and expiry date, marks the contract compliant and sets the next follow-up date before expiry, so the tracker will raise an alert when the policy is due to renew.

error.defect_description: Wrong expiry date keyed, giving a false or missed alert later.

next.condition: contract is enrolled in the protection program

evidence.note: Expiry dates drive the tracker's follow-up schedule. Shares are tier C.

steps.name: Cancel the protection program and credit the charges
steps.description: When a customer already enrolled sends a compliant certificate, the coordinator ends the program enrolment from the certificate's effective date, works out the program charges billed since then, sends billing an adjustment to credit them and stop future charges, and tells the customer by e-mail or letter.

error.defect_description: Credit calculated from the wrong date.

next.condition: credit goes back more than 60 days

evidence.note: Customary practice for lender-placed programs; the 60-day limit is an assumption.

steps.name: Approve a backdated credit of program charges
steps.description: The supervisor checks that the customer's own policy was in force for the whole period being credited, looks at whether any claim was paid under the program, and approves or limits the credit.

control.basis: Delegated authority for credits and refunds of program charges

evidence.note: Common approval control; times are estimates.

steps.name: Confirm insurance to funding
steps.description: For a truck or mid-ticket deal that cannot fund without a certificate, the coordinator marks the insurance condition cleared in the tracker and the origination portal and e-mails the funding specialist that the file can proceed.

control.basis: Funding conditions: trucks and mid-ticket equipment need insurance evidence before the vendor is paid

evidence.note: Certificates obtained before funding are documented in the prospectus and in efc-audit-and-fund-contracts s13.

steps.name: Send a deficiency request to the broker or customer
steps.description: The coordinator e-mails the insurance broker named on the certificate, or the customer when there is none, listing exactly what must change (loss payee wording and address, named insured, missing serial numbers, limit, expiry) and attaches the requirement letter.

error.defect_description: Request omits one of the deficiencies, so the corrected certificate is still wrong.

evidence.note: Estimate based on the certificate problems the organisation file describes.

steps.name: Broker or customer corrects the certificate
steps.description: The case waits for the broker to issue a corrected certificate or endorsement. Brokers with many small commercial accounts take days to weeks, and some customers forward the request to a broker who never received the first one.

evidence.note: Waiting time and reply rate are estimates.

steps.name: Chase the broker or customer
steps.description: When the follow-up date passes the coordinator calls or e-mails the broker and the customer again, confirms the right broker contact and resends the deficiency list.

evidence.note: Follow-up dates and notes on the tracker work schedule are documented; times are tier C.

steps.name: Broker or customer replies after the chase
steps.description: The case waits again for a corrected certificate. Without one the contract is treated as uninsured and moves to the final notice before program enrolment.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Check an expiry or cancellation alert
steps.description: For a policy the tracker shows as expired, or an insurer's cancellation notice, the coordinator checks whether a renewal certificate already arrived but was not indexed, whether the contract has been paid out or terminated, and whether the customer is already enrolled, then starts the notice cycle or closes the alert.

error.defect_description: A renewal already on file is missed and the customer gets a needless notice.

next.condition: renewal on file, contract ended or already enrolled

evidence.note: Tracking of expired policies and lapse notifications are documented; shares are tier C.

steps.name: Send the first notice asking for proof of insurance
steps.description: The tracker produces the day's batch of first notices (new contracts without a certificate and lapsed policies). The coordinator checks the batch for contracts that should not get one, releases it for printing and e-mail, and sets a follow-up date about 30 days out. The letter explains the requirement and that the equipment will be enrolled in the protection program with a monthly charge if no proof arrives.
inputs: lapse case or new contract without certificate

error.defect_description: Notice sent to an old address or for a paid-out contract.

evidence.note: Insurance letters from the tracker and automatic enrolment without proof are documented; the 30-day follow-up is tier C.

steps.name: Customer or broker responds to the first notice
steps.description: The case waits for the customer or broker to send a certificate. Many small businesses forward the letter to their broker late or ignore it.

next.condition: no response by the follow-up date

evidence.note: Response rate and timing are estimates.

steps.name: Send the final notice of program enrolment
steps.description: The coordinator releases the final notice from the tracker batch: the equipment will be enrolled in the protection program from a stated date, the monthly charge, the coverage and deductible, and how to avoid or cancel it by sending proof of insurance.

evidence.note: Program terms (automatic enrolment, deductible) are shown to customers; the notice content is tier C.

steps.name: Final notice period runs
steps.description: The case waits out the final notice period, usually two to four weeks, for the customer or broker to send a certificate before the enrolment date stated in the notice.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Enrol the contract in the protection program
steps.description: The coordinator enrols the equipment in the protection program in the tracker with the effective date and insured value, sets the monthly insurance charge in the lease system so it bills on the next invoice, and records the enrolment for the monthly report to the program insurer.

error.defect_description: Insured value or charge keyed wrongly.

control.basis: Lease insurance clause allowing the lessor to insure the equipment at the lessee's cost, and the program agreement with the protection program insurer

evidence.note: Automatic enrolment and lessor programs are documented; times are tier C.

steps.name: Answer a customer's call about the program charge
steps.description: When the charge appears on the invoice some customers call customer service. The representative explains the requirement and the charge from the contract notes and tracker status, and asks for a certificate by e-mail when the customer says they are insured, forwarding it to insurance tracking.

evidence.note: Based on efc-handle-service-requests s14, where representatives explain program charges and forward certificates; shares are estimates.

steps.name: Reconcile and send the monthly bordereau
steps.description: At month end the supervisor runs the list of enrolled contracts, values and premiums from the tracker, reconciles it to the insurance charges billed in the lease system, corrects differences and sends the bordereau to the program insurer through its portal or by e-mail.

control.basis: Program agreement with the insurer: complete monthly reporting of insured contracts and premiums, reconciled to billing

evidence.note: Monthly bordereau per the organisation file's process map; touch is per contract, the whole run takes several hours.

steps.name: Route a loss or damage report to lease administration
steps.description: When a customer or insurer reports that leased equipment was destroyed, stolen or damaged, the coordinator checks what cover is on file (customer policy or program), notes the claim, sends the casualty notice and the certificate or program details to lease administration and, for enrolled contracts, notifies the program insurer.

evidence.note: Hand-off to settle-casualty-losses per the organisation file; times are estimates.

exceptions.name: Deficient certificate
exceptions.description: Wrong named insured, additional insured instead of loss payee, missing serial numbers or too low a limit; the broker is asked for a corrected certificate and chased.

exceptions.name: Waiver or non-standard coverage
exceptions.description: Blanket fleet policies, high deductibles or self-insurance need the supervisor's approval.

exceptions.name: Enrolled customer later proves insurance
exceptions.description: The program is cancelled from the certificate's effective date and the charges are credited; long backdating needs approval.

exceptions.name: Uninsured contract enrolled in the program
exceptions.description: No proof after the first and final notices; the contract is enrolled and the charge billed, and some customers call to dispute it.

exceptions.name: Loss reported
exceptions.description: A destroyed, stolen or damaged unit is routed to lease administration with the coverage details.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from receipt of the certificate, booking or alert to coverage recorded, program enrolment reported or case closed
benchmarks.population: Author's estimate for in-house insurance tracking at a mid-size lessor

evidence.note: Most cases are certificate reviews and set-ups finished within days; lapse cases run through a 30-day first notice, a two-to-four week final notice and a month-end bordereau. No published benchmark was found.

benchmarks.population: National Bank equipment financing loss damage waiver

benchmarks.unit: leased assets tracked for the life of the agreement

evidence.note: Shows the scale at which tracking is outsourced.

benchmarks.unit: share of certificates reviewed that need correction

evidence.note: Estimate; the organisation file notes wrong insureds and omitted equipment are common.

pain_points.description: Certificates commonly name the wrong business, show the company only as additional insured, or describe the equipment vaguely, so a third of reviews end in a deficiency request and a broker chase.

evidence.note: Wording problems from the source; the share is tier C.

pain_points.description: Lapse cases take one to two months of letters and waiting, during which the equipment may be uninsured and the company exposed to an unrecoverable loss.

evidence.note: Lessors often do not know whether equipment is insured; timing is tier C.

pain_points.description: Program charges appear on invoices of customers who were insured but never sent proof, causing calls, credits and complaints.

evidence.note: Common source of service calls per efc-handle-service-requests.

pain_points.description: The inbox and work schedule build backlogs at renewal peaks; certificates matched to the wrong contract or not indexed trigger needless lapse notices.

evidence.note: Estimate.

sources.title: Insurance Tracking module [U13]
sources.supports: A lease system's insurance tracking module keeps track of expired policies, builds a daily work schedule of accounts for each clerk (lease, lessee, policy number, expiry date, follow-up date, note), starts tracking a set number of days before expiry, assigns accounts to clerks in the end-of-period run, lets supervisors reassign work, and prints the clerk's details on insurance letters.

sources.title: Commercial equipment: insurance tracking
sources.supports: Insurance tracking for equipment lessors runs for the full term of the agreement, gives status notifications for tracked policies and updates on lapsed or expired coverage, and the provider handles the communication needed to get a new policy placed after a lapse.

sources.title: Equipment financing (specialty equipment insurance)
sources.supports: Insurance tracking monitors coverage status and detects uninsured assets, included in embedded programs for lessors or offered alone; physical damage cover for leased equipment is offered across the United States and Canada.

sources.title: Equipment financing: vehicle protection plan
sources.supports: A Canadian equipment lessor's loss damage waiver covers eligible leased equipment for a fee; if the customer does not provide proof of external insurance the equipment is automatically enrolled; the deductible is $250.

sources.title: Insurance protection for secured lenders
sources.supports: Certificates often name lenders as additional insured or loss payee without the mortgagee wording that gives full protection; lenders should check that the policy itself, not only the certificate, names them correctly; Builders Capital v. Aviva (2022 ABCA 120) left lenders unprotected when the policy named the wrong party.

sources.title: Industry forms
sources.publisher: Centre for Study of Insurance Operations (CSIO)
sources.supports: CSIO maintains standard forms for the Canadian property and casualty industry, including a Certificate of Property Insurance and a Certificate of Liability Insurance used by brokers.

sources.title: Charter Equipment Lease 1998-1 LLC prospectus (Form 424B1)
sources.supports: A New York and Toronto lessor requires property insurance against damage, fire, theft and other loss for the replacement value of the equipment with the lessor as loss payee, and public liability insurance naming the lessor as additional insured; clients use their own carrier or, for strong credits, self-insurance; the contract administrator obtains insurance certificates before funding. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/ by earlier work.

sources.title: Why keeping track of asset finance agreements can feel like wading through fog
sources.supports: When the customer must insure leased equipment, lessors very often have no real idea whether it is actually or adequately insured; tracking is a cumbersome, resource-heavy task that outsourcing can relieve.

assumptions: The four coordinators and one supervisor of the organisation file's insurance tracking unit do this work in-house; many lessors outsource it to tracking vendors, which would remove most of the coordinator steps.
Each certificate or lapse case is one case. A certificate that arrives in answer to a notice or a deficiency request is handled inside the open case, not counted again as a new case.

Lapse cases are started by the tracker's expiry date or an insurer's cancellation notice; they are attributed to insurer in interfaces.triggered_by because the organisation file has no internal trigger for expiry.

About 14% of cases (roughly 600 a month) end in program enrolment and about 6% in a program cancellation. Shares of work types, the 32% deficiency rate, response rates to notices and the 30-day and 2-to-4-week notice periods are the author's estimates. No Canadian rule fixes the notice periods for commercial equipment.

Insurance confirmations to funding (about 3% of cases, roughly 130 a month) exceed the 3% share of fundings that efc-audit-and-fund-contracts attributes to them (about 42 a month), because most confirmations are simply on file when funding checks the tracker.

Licensing rules for a lessor that offers an insurance program to its customers (for example Quebec's distribution without a representative) were not researched; the program is assumed to be offered through the insurer's program agreement.

Mean hands-on time is about 11 minutes per case including rework loops, about 6 FTE in total (about 5 of it coordinator time) at 4,400 cases a month against the four coordinators and one supervisor in the organisation file. The unit is stretched at the mode and clearly short at the 5,300-case high end, which matches the backlogs common in in-house tracking; this is recorded as a possible understatement of headcount in the organisation file.
Loaded hourly costs are the organisation file's (wage times 1.35).
